questions.q_text: Because Mr. Chang has been busy these days, it's _______ whether he will come to the party.

options.D: inevitable

explanation.translation: 因為張先生最近很忙，所以他是否會來參加派對還很令人懷疑。
explanation.technique: 看到空格後面的 whether (是否)，就知道這件事充滿「不確定性」。選項中只有 doubtful (懷疑的) 帶有不確定的語氣。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) unlikely (不太可能的)：通常接 to V 或 that 子句，不會接 whether。
❌ (B) impossible (不可能的)：語氣太絕對，與 whether 矛盾。
✅ (C) doubtful (令人懷疑的)：完美契合 whether 表達的不確定性。
❌ (D) inevitable (無可避免的)：語意完全相反。
explanation.roots: in- (否定) + evit (避免) + -able (可以...的) ➔ 無可避免的
collocations: it is doubtful whether / that... (令人懷疑是否...)
sentences: It is highly doubtful whether the project will be finished on time. (專案能否準時完成令人高度懷疑。)
explanation.summary: 【It is doubtful whether/if + S + V】是常考句型，表示對某事抱持懷疑。

questions.q_text: I'm quite _______ to the weather in Taiwan, so I think I'll stay here for another year.

options.D: accustomed

explanation.translation: 我相當習慣台灣的天氣，所以我想我會在這裡多待一年。
explanation.technique: 觀察空格後的介系詞 to，搭配後半句「所以想多待一年」，推斷出是對天氣「習慣」。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) devoted to (致力於)：人不可能「奉獻給」天氣，邏輯不通。
❌ (B) satisfied (滿意)：需搭配 with。
❌ (C) pleased (高興)：需搭配 with。
✅ (D) accustomed to (習慣於...)：符合文法與語意。
explanation.roots: ac- (朝向) + custom (習慣) + -ed (形容詞) ➔ 習慣於...
collocations: be / get accustomed to + N/Ving (漸漸習慣於...)
sentences: She quickly became accustomed to his strange sleeping schedule. (她很快就習慣了他的睡眠作息。)
explanation.summary: 【be accustomed to + V-ing/N】與【be used to + V-ing/N】為同義詞，to 都是介系詞！

questions.q_text: Mr. Smith won't tolerate talking during class; he says it _______ others.

options.A: disturbs

explanation.translation: Smith 先生不容許上課講話；他說這會打擾到其他人。
explanation.technique: 上課講話會對別人造成什麼影響？自然是「打擾 (disturb)」。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) disturb (打擾)：符合語境。
❌ (B) deserve (應得)：放此處語意不通。
❌ (C) destroy (摧毀)：語氣過重。
❌ (D) dismiss (解散)：講話不會解散別人。
explanation.roots: dis- (完全) + turb (攪亂) ➔ 完全攪亂 ➔ 打擾
sentences: He worked hard and deserves a promotion. (他工作努力，理應獲得升職。)
explanation.summary: 必背單字 tolerate (容忍) 後面喜歡接 V-ing。

questions.q_text: On the basis of the clues, can you predict the _______ of the story?

options.A: outcome

explanation.translation: 根據這些線索，你能預測故事的結果(結局)嗎？
explanation.technique: 能針對「故事 (story)」去「預測 (predict)」的，通常是「結局或結果 (outcome)」。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) outcome (結果/結局)：與 predict 搭配。
❌ (B) headline (新聞標題)：故事沒有標題。
❌ (C) cause (原因)：通常是根據結果推原因。
❌ (D) performance (表現)：與推斷無關。
explanation.roots: pre- (在...之前) + dict (說) ➔ 預言/預測
sentences: It is difficult to predict the final outcome of the election. (很難預測選舉的最終結果。)
explanation.summary: dict 是「說」的字根，延伸字必背：dictator (獨裁者)、dictionary (字典)。

questions.q_text: A good reader can often figure out what new words mean by using _______.

options.B: context

explanation.translation: 一個好的閱讀者通常能透過使用上下文來推斷新單字的意思。
explanation.technique: 推斷單字意思 (figure out what new words mean) 唯一的方法就是看「上下文 (context)」。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) contact (接觸)：keep in contact。
✅ (B) context (上下文)：閱讀測驗必備技巧。
❌ (C) content (內容)：指書本的目錄或內文。
❌ (D) contest (比賽)：speech contest。
explanation.roots: con- (共同) + text (編織) ➔ 共同編織成的文章 ➔ 上下文
collocations: out of context (脫離上下文/斷章取義)
sentences: You shouldn't quote my words out of context. (你不該斷章取義地引用我的話。)
explanation.summary: figure out 等於 understand / comprehend (推斷出/理解)。

questions.q_text: I wonder why she _______ turned up the radio when I was studying.

options.A: sympathetically
options.C: deliberately
options.D: thoroughly

explanation.translation: 我想知道為什麼當我在讀書時，她要故意把收音機開大聲。
explanation.technique: 「我在讀書」，別人卻「把收音機開大聲」，這是一種帶有惡意、故意的行為。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) sympathetically (同情地)：不合邏輯。
❌ (B) primarily (主要地)：語意不符。
✅ (C) deliberately (故意地)：等於 on purpose。
❌ (D) thoroughly (徹底地)：修飾打掃或檢查。
explanation.roots: de- (加強) + liber (秤/衡量) + -ate ➔ 仔細衡量過才做 ➔ 故意地
sentences: He deliberately ignored my question. (他故意忽略我的問題。)
explanation.summary: 「故意地」三兄弟必背：deliberately = intentionally = on purpose。

questions.q_text: It suddenly _______ me that I had to get to the airport to meet a friend.

options.B: struck

explanation.translation: 我突然想起我必須去機場接朋友。
explanation.technique: 表示「突然想起」有兩種說法，空格後「直接接 me」的是 strike；如果選 occur，後面必須加 to。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) took：It took me 後面需接時間或金錢。
✅ (B) struck：It strikes sb. that... (某人突然想起)。
❌ (C) occurred：必須寫成 It occurred **to** me that...。
❌ (D) surprised：語意不對。
explanation.roots: strike (打擊) ➔ 像被雷打到一樣 ➔ 突然想起
collocations: It strikes/hit someone that... (某人突然想到...)
sentences: It never occurred to him to ask for help. (他從未想過要求救。)
explanation.summary: 【某人突然想到某事】：It strikes someone that... = It occurs to someone that...

questions.q_text: Being a very careful person, he is quite _______ in giving his comments.

options.A: reserved
options.B: melancholy

explanation.translation: 身為一個非常謹慎的人，他在給予評論時相當保留(謹言慎行)。
explanation.technique: 前半句的 careful person (謹慎的人) 就是線索。謹慎的人講話自然會比較「保留/拘謹 (reserved)」。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) reserved (保留的)：符合謹慎之人的說話特質。
❌ (B) melancholy (憂鬱的)：謹慎不代表憂鬱。
❌ (C) complicated (複雜的)：用來形容事情。
❌ (D) generous (慷慨的)：不搭配 comments。
explanation.roots: re- (向後) + serve (保持) ➔ 把話留在後面不說 ➔ 謹言慎行
sentences: English people are often thought of as being quite reserved. (英國人常被認為相當拘謹。)
explanation.summary: reserve 當動詞是「預約/保留」，加上 ed 變形容詞，引申為人的個性「內向的」。

questions.q_text: Most viewers agreed that the movie _______ was not as good as the book.

options.B: version

explanation.translation: 大多數觀眾同意這部電影版本不如原著小說好看。
explanation.technique: 比較「電影 (movie)」和「小說(the book)」，我們會說 movie version (電影改編版本)。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) routine (例行公事)：無此說法。
✅ (B) version (版本)：專指軟體、書籍、電影的「版本」。
❌ (C) copy (複製品)：書的一本叫 a copy，但電影改編不叫 copy。
❌ (D) issue (期號)：雜誌的一期叫 issue。
explanation.roots: vers (轉) + -ion ➔ 原著轉換出來的東西 ➔ 改編版本
collocations: a controversial issue (具爭議的議題)
sentences: I prefer the original version of this song. (我比較喜歡這首歌的原唱版本。)
explanation.summary: as + 形容詞原級 + as ... 是一個必考比較句型，意為「和...一樣好/不好」。

questions.q_text: The native greeted the travelers in a _______ language which was strange to them.

options.C: peculiar

explanation.translation: 當地人用一種對旅客來說很陌生的奇怪語言向他們打招呼。
explanation.technique: 後面的 which was strange to them 提供了直接線索。strange (奇怪的) 的高階同義詞就是 peculiar。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) contrary (相反的)：on the contrary。
❌ (B) relative (相對的)：無法修飾 strange 語言。
✅ (C) peculiar (奇怪的/特有的)：與 strange 同義。
❌ (D) spiral (螺旋的)：語言不會是螺旋的。
explanation.roots: pecul (私有財產) + -iar ➔ 只有某地區自己有的 ➔ 特有的/奇怪的
sentences: This type of building is peculiar to the south of the country. (這種建築是該國南部所特有的。)
explanation.summary: 當作「特有的」解釋時，必背片語：be peculiar to (某地所獨有的)。

groups.passage:
The umbrella is not a new invention. The Chinese [BLANK_11] umbrellas in the eleventh century B.C. [BLANK_12] China they traveled to India, Persia, and Egypt. But in Greece and Rome, men [BLANK_13] use them. They believed umbrellas were [BLANK_14] for women.

When the Spanish explorers went to Mexico, they saw the Aztec kings [BLANK_15] umbrellas. English explorers found out that Indian princes also carried umbrellas on the east coast of North America. It [BLANK_16] that people in different parts of the world invented umbrellas at different times.

England was probably the first country in Europe [BLANK_17] ordinary people used umbrellas [BLANK_18] the rain. England has a rainy climate, and umbrellas are very useful there.

The umbrella is now a very ordinary [BLANK_19]. Everybody uses it today. It keeps the rain and the sun off people. Some umbrellas fold up, [BLANK_20] it is easy to carry them.
groups.passage_translation:
雨傘並不是一項新發明。中國人在西元前十一世紀就已經有了雨傘。從中國，雨傘傳到了印度、波斯和埃及。但是在希臘和羅馬，男人是不會使用雨傘的。他們認為雨傘只是給女人用的。

當西班牙探險家前往墨西哥時，他們看到阿茲特克的國王正在使用雨傘。英國探險家也發現在北美洲東岸的印第安王子也會攜帶雨傘。似乎世界各地的人們在不同的時間都發明了雨傘。

英國可能是歐洲第一個由普通百姓撐傘來擋雨的國家。英國的氣候多雨，所以雨傘在那裡非常實用。

雨傘現在是一件非常普遍的物品。今天每個人都在使用它。它可以為人們擋雨遮陽。有些雨傘可以折疊，所以很容易攜帶。

explanation.technique: 看到 in the eleventh century B.C. 這種「明確的過去時間」，動詞必須秒選「過去簡單式」。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) have had：現在完成式，需搭配 for/since。
✅ (B) had：過去簡單式，精準表達過去的事實。
❌ (C) have：現在簡單式，時態不對。
explanation.summary: 時間副詞決定時態！只要看到 in + 過去時間 (如 in 1990)，動詞 100% 選過去式。

explanation.technique: 觀察後面的動詞 traveled to India (傳播/旅行到印度)，得知有一個出發的起點，故選 From。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) From：表示起點，「從中國出發」。
❌ (B) In：表示在中國內，不符句意。
explanation.summary: 【From A to B】從A到B，是表達事物傳播、位移的最基本介系詞搭配。

explanation.technique: 後一句說「他們認為雨傘是給女人用的」，代表這是一種刻板印象，因此男人是「絕對不肯/不會」用傘的。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (B) could：表能力，他們不是不能撐傘，是不肯。
✅ (C) wouldn't：will not 的過去式，表示過去的「強烈拒絕」或「不肯」。
❌ (D) won't：時態錯誤。
explanation.summary: 助動詞 would 除了表示「將會」，在否定時 wouldn't 常帶有「死都不肯 / 拒絕」的語氣。

explanation.technique: 配合上文男人不用傘，代表在當時的觀念裡，雨傘是「唯一 (only)」女性專屬的物品。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (B) only：僅僅、只有 (only for women 專屬於女性)。
❌ (A/C/D)：likely (可能)、nearly (幾乎)、possibly (可能)，皆無法表達排他性語氣。
explanation.summary: only 常用來強調唯一性，only for + 族群 也是極為常見的搭配。

explanation.technique: 【感官動詞必考句型】：看到 saw，就要想到「看見某人正在做某事」：saw + O + Ving 或 原形V。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (B) to use：感官動詞後方絕對不能接 to V。
✅ (D) using：符合感官動詞 + O + Ving 的文法，表達「看到國王『正在』撐傘」。
explanation.summary: 三大感官動詞 see, hear, watch 必背：後方受詞補語只能接 原形V 或 V-ing。

explanation.technique: 看到 It _______ that... 的句型，第一個要反射性想到 It seems that... (似乎/看起來...) 的虛主詞句型。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) seems：It seems that S+V 是鐵則句型。
❌ (C) looks：look 通常接 like (It looks like...)。
explanation.summary: 寫作超級好用的句型：It seems that + 子句 (似乎...)，可讓語氣更客觀。

explanation.technique: 先行詞為 country (地方)，且後面的子句結構非常完整，沒有缺主詞或受詞，因此必須用「關係副詞 where」。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (D) where：修飾地方，且引導完整子句。
❌ (C) which：若用 which，後方子句必須不完整 (缺主詞或受詞)。
explanation.summary: 判斷關代 which 和關副 where 的不二法門：看後方子句是否完整！完整選 where，不完整選 which。

explanation.technique: 普通人使用雨傘來「抵擋」雨水。介系詞 against 有「防禦、對抗」的意思。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (C) against：use umbrellas against the rain (撐傘禦雨)。
❌ (D) from：若用 from，通常搭配 protect (protect us from the rain)。
explanation.summary: against 是一個充滿戰鬥氣息的介系詞，表示「對抗、防禦」，例如 fight against。

explanation.technique: 雨傘是一個具體的實體「物品」，選項中只有 object 適合指稱實體物。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) subject：主題/科目。
✅ (B) object：物體/物品。
❌ (C) matter：物質/事件。
explanation.summary: object 在高中英文有兩大意思：1. 物品 (實體)；2. 反對 (動詞, object to + N)。

explanation.technique: 前句為「原因」(可折疊)，後句為「結果」(容易攜帶)，表因果關係的對等連接詞秒選 so。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) so：所以，表達順暢的因果邏輯。
❌ (B) for：當連接詞表「因為」，放這裡邏輯顛倒。
explanation.summary: 不要小看 so (所以) 和 for (因為) 這兩個對等連接詞，在克漏字中它們是判斷邏輯方向的明燈。

groups.passage: A person's self-concept is reflected in the way he or she behaves, and the way a person behaves affects other people's reactions. [BLANK_21], the way people think about themselves [BLANK_22] a profound effect on all areas of their lives. For instance, people who have a [BLANK_23] sense of self-esteem usually act with confidence. [BLANK_24] they have self-assurance, they do not need constant praise and encouragement from others to feel [BLANK_25] about themselves. Self-confident people are their own best friends. They participate [BLANK_26] life enthusiastically and spontaneously. They are not affected by [BLANK_27] others think they "should" do. People [BLANK_28] high self-esteem are not hurt by criticism; they do not [BLANK_29] criticism as personal rejection. [BLANK_30], they tend to believe criticism to be suggestion for improvement.
groups.passage_translation: 一個人的自我概念反映在他或她的行為方式上，而一個人的行為方式又會影響其他人的反應。總的來說，人們對自己的看法對他們生活的各個領域都有深遠的影響。例如，具有正面自尊感的人通常表現得很有自信。因為他們有自信，所以不需要別人不斷的讚美和鼓勵就能對自己感覺良好。自信的人是自己最好的朋友。他們熱情且自發地參與生活。他們不會受到別人認為他們「應該」做什麼的影響。擁有高自尊的人不會被批評傷害；他們不會把批評視為對個人的拒絕。相反地，他們傾向於相信批評是為了改進的建議。

explanation.technique: 前面講了兩句客觀心理學事實，此處需要一個副詞片語來做「總結」，故選 In general。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (C) In general：一般而言 / 總的來說。非常適合作為引言後的總結。
❌ (D) Even so：即使如此 (表讓步轉折)。
explanation.summary: 作文神兵利器 In general = Generally speaking (總的來說)，放在句首可讓語氣看起來極具權威感。

explanation.technique: 【主動詞一致】：真正的單數主詞是 the way，後面的子句是修飾它的。單數主詞要配單數動詞 has。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (A) have：複數動詞，錯誤。
✅ (D) has：與單數主詞 the way 完美呼應。
explanation.summary: 常考搭配詞：have a profound effect on... (對...有深遠的影響)。

explanation.technique: 後文說他們表現得充滿自信 (with confidence)，可見這是一種「正向的 (positive)」自尊。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) positive：正面的/積極的。
❌ (C) weak：脆弱的 (邏輯相反)。
explanation.summary: positive thinking (正向思考) 與 negative attitude (消極態度) 是高中大考閱測常客。

explanation.technique: 「有自信」是原因，「不需要別人讚美」是結果。這是一個完美的因果關係。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (B) Because：因為。引導原因副詞子句。
❌ (D) However：然而 (副詞，不能連接兩個子句)。
explanation.summary: However 是副詞，後面要打逗號，絕對不能像 Because 一樣當連接詞串聯兩個句子！

explanation.technique: feel 是連綴動詞，後方要接形容詞。feel good about oneself 是一個固定的心理學搭配，表示「對自己感覺良好」。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (C) well：當形容詞時專指「身體健康」，不適用於心理狀態。
✅ (D) good：feel good about oneself 完美契合語境。
explanation.summary: feel well 指的是你沒生病；feel good 才是指你心情好或對自己有自信。

explanation.technique: participate in (參與) 是高中英文絕對要刻在骨子裡的固定搭配詞！
explanation.analysis: ✅ (C) in：participate 永遠綁定 in。
explanation.summary: 【參與的三大片語】：participate in = take part in = join in。

explanation.technique: 介系詞 by 後面必須接名詞子句。觀察 do 後面缺了受詞 (做「什麼」)，所以要填入複合關係代名詞 what。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (D) what：等於 the things which，完美補足動詞 do 缺少的受詞。
❌ (A) which：前面沒有先行詞。
explanation.summary: what 引導的名詞子句具備「雙重身份」：既當前面介系詞的受詞，又當後面動詞的受詞。

explanation.technique: 這裡要修飾名詞 People，因為本句已經有主要動詞 (are not hurt)，所以這裡只能填介系詞。with 表「擁有、帶有」。
explanation.analysis:
❌ (D) have：若放 have 就會有兩個主要動詞，文法大錯。
✅ (C) with：People with high self-esteem (帶有高自尊的人)。
explanation.summary: 介系詞 with 常常等於 who have，用來精簡句子結構。例如：a girl with long hair。

explanation.technique: 看到空格後面有一個關鍵的 as，你的直覺就該大喊：regard A as B (把 A 視為 B)！
explanation.analysis:
✅ (D) regard：搭配 as 組成黃金片語。
❌ (B) look：必須搭配 at，look upon A as B 才對。
explanation.summary: 【視 A 為 B 大集合】：regard A as B = see A as B = view A as B = think of A as B。

explanation.technique: 前一句是「否定狀態」(they do NOT...)，後一句提出「相反的正面做法」，這時最適合用轉折副詞 Instead。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (A) Instead：承接上文的否定，帶出他們實際的積極作為。
❌ (B) In addition：此外 (表遞進)。
explanation.summary: Instead 是一個非常棒的起手式，用來告訴閱卷老師：「我不是要這樣做，『相反地』我要那樣做」。

groups.passage:
Most heroes are people like you. But what makes them heroes? They find special courage when they need it. They are brave enough to help in an emergency while others may stand by. A hero sees what needs to be done and does it.

Sometimes heroes are rewarded for their brave acts. One such reward is the Carnegie Medal. It is given to people who act bravely and face danger to save the lives of others.

The medal was named after Andrew Carnegie. In 1886, Carnegie heard about a young man by the name of William Hunter who lost his life trying to save two other boys from drowning. Carnegie became a very rich businessman and set aside money to honor heroes like William.
groups.passage_translation:
大多數的英雄都是像你我一樣的普通人。但到底是什麼讓他們成為英雄呢？他們在需要的時候會找到特別的勇氣。在緊急情況下，當其他人可能只會袖手旁觀時，他們卻夠勇敢去幫忙。英雄看見需要被完成的事情，並且付諸實行。

有時候，英雄們會因為他們的勇敢行為而獲得獎勵。其中一項獎勵就是卡內基獎章。它是頒發給那些勇敢行動，並面對危險以拯救他人生命的人。

這枚獎章是以安德魯·卡內基的名字命名的。在1886年，卡內基聽說了一位名叫威廉·亨特的年輕人，他為了救另外兩個快溺水的男孩而失去了自己的生命。卡內基後來成為了一位非常富有的商人，並撥出一筆錢來表揚像威廉這樣的英雄。

questions.q_text: The Carnegie Medal is given to those who are _______

explanation.technique: 題目問 given to those who...，對應文章第二段最後一句「save the lives of others (救別人=無私)」。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (D) 文章指出獎章頒給冒險救人的人，這正展現了 unselfish (無私) 與 courageous (勇敢) 的特質。 ❌ (C) 雖然勇敢，但沒有限制必須是 young (年輕的)。
explanation.summary: courage (勇氣) 的形容詞是 courageous，字尾 ous 代表「充滿...的」。

questions.q_text: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: William Hunter was a very brave boy.
options.C: Some heroes have been rewarded for their bravery.
options.D: Carnegie was a rich businessman and liked to help people.

explanation.technique: 主旨題看每段的第一句話。第一段講英雄定義，第二段破題「英雄會獲得獎勵 (rewarded)」，第三段舉卡內基為例。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (C) 貫穿全文，首段講英雄特質，後段介紹卡內基獎章如何「獎勵英雄的勇敢」。 ❌ (A/D) 只涵蓋了第三段的局部細節，不能代表全文主旨。
explanation.summary: 主旨題 (main idea) 切忌選「太過細節 (too specific)」的選項，例如 A 和 D。

questions.q_text: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.B: Brave deeds can take many different forms.
options.C: Over 6,000 people are Carnegie Medal recipients.
options.D: Some heroes have received money as well as the Medal.

explanation.technique: 這題是找錯誤選項。定位 Carnegie 和 Hunter 的關係。文章第三段寫 'heard about' (聽說過)。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (A) 文章說 Carnegie 'heard about' (聽說過) Hunter，代表他們並不認識 (not in person)。此為錯誤敘述，故選A。
explanation.summary: in person 是一個很常考的片語，意思是「親自 / 面對面地」。

groups.passage:
On May 26, 1977, George Willig traveled to the top of the 1,350-foot-tall World Trade Center in New York City. He did not take the elevator, however. Instead, like a human fly, George Willig climbed the outside of the immense 110-story building. His climb, which began at 6:30 a.m., took three and a half hours to finish.

At the top, Willig was greeted by both police and reporters. Some of the police officers asked him for his autograph. Then they wanted to put him in jail and charged him with violation of law for climbing the building without a permit.

By the next day, city officials had reevaluated the situation... Beame announced that the city would not punish "The Human Fly." Instead, he would be fined a penny for each of the 110 floors he had climbed.
groups.passage_translation:
1977年5月26日，喬治·威利格到了紐約市1350英尺高的世貿中心頂樓。然而，他沒有搭乘電梯。相反地，他就像一隻「人蠅」一樣，徒手攀爬了這棟高達110層樓的巨大建築的外部。他的攀登行動從早上6點30分開始，花了三個半小時才完成。

到達頂樓時，迎接威利格的是警察和記者。有些警察甚至向他要了簽名。但隨後他們就想把他關進監獄，並以無照攀爬建築物而指控他違法...

到了第二天，市府官員重新評估了情況。市長宣布不會懲罰「人蠅」。相反地，他每爬一層樓只被象徵性地罰款一便士。

questions.q_text: George Willig reached the top of the World Trade Center in New York at

explanation.technique: 這是簡單的數學計算題！定位第一段最後一句：6:30 a.m. 開始，花了三個半小時 (3.5 hours)。
explanation.analysis: 早上 6:30 + 3.5小時 = 早上 10 點 (ten o'clock in the morning)，故選 C。

questions.q_text: This passage is a story about

options.A: a man who enjoys dangers and risks.
options.B: a human being who can fly like a fly.
options.C: a man who has escaped from the jail.
options.D: a fly which climbs like a human being.

explanation.technique: 文章描述一個男人徒手攀爬 110 層高樓，明顯是在描述一個喜歡冒險的人。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (A) 關於一個享受危險與冒險的男人。 ❌ (B)與(D)的 fly 只是修辭(human fly)，不是真的蒼蠅。

questions.q_text: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.B: Willig was sent to prison for a year.
options.C: Willig was honored in a party and fined only $1.10.
options.D: Willig climbed the World Trade Center with permission.

explanation.technique: 定位文章最後一句：fined a penny for each of the 110 floors (110層樓，每層罰 1 便士，共 110 便士 = 1.10 美元)。
explanation.analysis:
✅ (C) 市長不但沒懲罰他，反而每層樓只罰一便士(共$1.10)。
❌ (A) 這是原本預計起訴的金額，後來並未執行。
❌ (D) 文章說他 without a permit (未經許可)。

groups.passage:
Printing is one of the most important means of communication. Without it you would not now be reading this passage. Even the development of radio and television has not diminished the importance of printing.

The first printing was done from wood blocks one letter at a time by hand. This was a slow process, requiring much skill and patience... A great step forward was the use of movable type. The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century...

One of the first European books to be printed in movable type was Johannes Gutenberg's 42-line Bible. The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy. It was printed in Flanders in 1474 by an Englishman, William Caxton...
groups.passage_translation:
印刷術是最重要的通訊方式之一。沒有它，你現在就不會讀到這篇文章。即使是廣播和電視的發展，也沒有削弱印刷術的重要性。

最早的印刷是用木塊手工一次刻一個字母。這是一個緩慢的過程，需要大量的技巧和耐心... 向前邁出的一大步是活字印刷的使用。中國人在11世紀發現了這個技術...

歐洲第一批用活字印刷的書籍之一是約翰尼斯·谷登堡的四十二行聖經。第一本同樣用活字印刷的英文書是關於特洛伊的歷史。它是由英國人威廉·卡克斯頓於1474年在法蘭德斯印刷的...

questions.q_text: Printing is important because

options.B: it has made reading books possible.
options.C: it has helped to develop radio and television.
options.D: William Caxton printed 80 books in English.

explanation.technique: 定位第一段第二句：Without it you would not now be reading this passage (沒有它你就讀不到這文章)。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (B) 印刷術讓閱讀書籍成為可能。

questions.q_text: The use of movable type was first introduced by

explanation.technique: 尋找關鍵字 movable type，定位第二段最後一句：The Chinese discovered this...。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (D) 第二段指出 The Chinese discovered this in the 11th century。

questions.q_text: According to the passage, the use of movable type was considered as a "great step forward" because

options.A: it did not need a lot of wood.
options.B: it required less skill and patience.
options.C: the printing letters could be reused.
options.D: every page of every book required individual carving.

explanation.technique: 相比於 wood blocks (木板一次只能刻一頁)，活字印刷(movable type) 的精髓就是字母可以移動重組(rearranged)來重複使用。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (C) 因為舊方法每頁都要獨立雕刻，而活字印刷可以重新排列字母(reused)。

questions.q_text: The first English book printed in movable type was

options.A: done from wood blocks one letter at a time.
options.B: done in a printing press at Westminster.

explanation.technique: 尋找關鍵字 first book... in English，定位第三段第二句。
explanation.analysis: ✅ (D) 第三段提到 The first book to be printed likewise in English was about the history of Troy。

For many years, people thought the [BLANK_41] of smoking were [BLANK_42] to smokers. But new studies have found that smoke from cigarettes can be [BLANK_43] to non-smokers too.

In December 1987, a U.S. Government report [BLANK_44] that non-smokers could risk getting lung cancer from [BLANK_45] in other people's cigarette smoke.

Another study looked at non-smoking [BLANK_46] athletes who had smoking parents or friends. Being [BLANK_47] cigarette smoke hurt the athletes' lungs, and made them [BLANK_48] more than athletes who did not have smokers close [BLANK_49], the study said. Studies like these have promoted the banning of smoking in [BLANK_50] places.
groups.passage_translation: 多年來，人們認為吸菸的損害僅限於吸菸者。但新的研究發現，香菸的煙霧對非吸菸者也可能是有害的... (略)

explanation.technique: the 後面必接名詞，且後方動詞為 were (複數)，選 damages (損害)。
explanation.analysis: 需要複數名詞作為 thought 子句的主詞。damages 符合吸菸造成的負面影響。
explanation.summary: damage 作為不可數名詞指「破壞」；加上 s 變成 damages 時，常指「賠償金」或多重的損害。

explanation.technique: 【必背搭配詞】：be limited to + N (侷限於...)，此處指損害僅限於吸菸者本身。
explanation.analysis: 看到後面的 to smokers，就該反射性選出 limited。
explanation.summary: be limited to / be restricted to (受限於...)，這兩個片語是閱讀與寫作必備。

explanation.technique: 前一句說只對吸菸者有害，But 轉折後，表示二手菸對非吸菸者也有「害 (harmful)」。
explanation.analysis: be harmful to (對...有害)，填入形容詞 harmful 完美契合文法。
explanation.summary: be harmful to = do harm to，都是表達「對...造成傷害」的極佳寫法。

explanation.technique: 主詞 a U.S. Government report 後面缺了動詞，且要帶出 that 子句。故選過去式動詞 indicated (指出)。
explanation.analysis: indicated 符合報告「指出/表明」事實的語境。
explanation.summary: report indicated / showed / revealed that... 是引述報告結果的黃金動詞群。

explanation.technique: 介系詞 from 後面要接 V-ing。吸菸的動作是 breathing in (吸入)。
explanation.analysis: 選 breathing 配合 in other people's cigarette smoke (吸入別人的煙)。
explanation.summary: breathe (動詞) 字尾有 e；breath (名詞) 沒有 e，發音也完全不同，千萬別搞混！

explanation.technique: 空格在名詞 athletes 前，需填入形容詞修飾。
explanation.analysis: teenage (青少年的) 修飾運動員，符合文意。

explanation.technique: Being 後方接地方副詞片語，表示「處於...附近」。
explanation.analysis: near (靠近) cigarette smoke，符合二手菸情境。

explanation.technique: 使役動詞 make + 受詞 + 原形動詞。
explanation.analysis: 原形動詞 cough (咳嗽) 符合抽二手菸的生理反應。

explanation.technique: close by 為地方副詞片語，表示「在附近」。
explanation.analysis: 介系詞 by 與 close 搭配。

explanation.technique: public places (公共場所) 為固定搭配名詞組。
explanation.analysis: 形容詞 public 修飾 places。

questions.q_text: 對於什麼是最佳的渡假方式，大家都有不同的看法。
questions.answer: People have different opinions on what is the best way to spend a vacation.

explanation.technique: 「對...有不同看法」：have different opinions on/about...；「什麼是...」：疑問詞 what 引導名詞子句當作 on 的受詞。
explanation.analysis: 標準的「名詞子句當介系詞受詞」用法，這是大考翻譯必考重點。

questions.q_text: 有些人喜歡到寧靜的森林中去，在那兒他們可以暫時遠離人群。
questions.answer: Some people like to go to a quiet forest, where they can temporarily stay away from crowds.

explanation.technique: 「在那兒...」：使用關係副詞 where 引導形容詞子句補充說明森林。「暫時遠離人群」：temporarily stay away from crowds.
explanation.analysis: 此題考驗關係副詞 where 的運用，逗號後的 where 等於 and there。

questions.q_text: 有些人卻寧願到大都市去，因為他們可以參觀博物館或購物。
questions.answer: Some, however, would rather go to big cities because they can visit museums or go shopping.

explanation.technique: 「寧願...」：would rather + 原形動詞
explanation.analysis: 對比前面的 Some people，此處可用 Some, however，增加文章層次。

questions.q_text: 還有一些人喜歡到海邊去，讓海浪沖走他們的煩惱。
questions.answer: Still others like to go to the beach and let the waves wash away their worries.

explanation.technique: 「讓海浪沖走煩惱」：let (使役動詞) + the waves + wash away (原形動詞) + their worries.
explanation.analysis: 使役動詞 let 的受詞補語必須是原形動詞，這是國中到高中都不斷重複的超級大考點。

questions.q_text: 有少數人則決定留在家裡，做一些像打掃屋子之類的事。
questions.answer: A few people decide to stay at home and do things like cleaning the house.

explanation.technique: 「像...之類的事」：things like + V-ing
explanation.analysis: like 在此作為介系詞，後方動詞須加上 -ing 變動名詞。此處 cleaning the house 是動名詞片語。

groups.passage:
📝 英文作文寫作提示

【題目】
Things Are Not As Difficult As They Appear (事情不如表面看起來困難)

【說明】
在成長的過程中，有些事情在開始的時候你可能覺得很難，但經過一番努力後就不再認為因難了。請寫一篇至少一百二十個單字的英文作文，描述一個親身的經驗。

⚠️ 文章的頭兩句必須是：
Things are not as difficult as they appear. I have a personal experience to prove this.

questions.q_text: 請在右側作答區輸入您的作文，系統將為您統計字數。
questions.answer:
Things are not as difficult as they appear. I have a personal experience to prove this. When I first started learning how to swim, I was terrified of the water. Every time I stepped into the pool, my heart would race, and I felt like I was going to sink. It seemed impossible for me to float, let alone swim across the pool.

However, I didn't give up. I enrolled in a swimming class and practiced breathing underwater. My coach taught me how to relax my muscles. Gradually, after weeks of swallowing water and struggling, I finally managed to swim my first lap. Now, swimming is my favorite sport. This experience taught me that with persistence, any difficulty can be overcome.

explanation.technique:
【寫作架構指引】：
1. **破題與情境設定**：務必先抄寫規定的兩句話。接著挑選一個具體的技能（如學游泳、騎腳踏車、學樂器），強烈描述初學時的恐懼與挫折感，製造反差。
2. **轉折與行動**：用 However 或 Nevertheless 帶出你不放棄的行動（如報名課程、反覆練習），使用漸進式副詞（Gradually）。
3. **結論點題**：呼應首句，用一句有力的格言收尾，展現堅持的力量。
explanation.analysis:
【時態與句型提醒】：
- 描述過去經驗時必須全程使用「過去式」。
- 結論的體悟可以使用「現在式」表示真理。
sentences: It seemed impossible for me to float, let alone swim across the pool. (我似乎連漂浮都不可能，更不用說游過泳池了。)
explanation.summary: 必背寫作結尾金句：This experience taught me that with persistence, any difficulty can be overcome. (這段經驗教會我，只要堅持，任何困難都能被克服。)
